audit.why: 51.24% over 3105 games. Vex owns levels 1-5, Ahri takes level 6 on Spirit Rush, Vex retakes first item and two items. Difficulty 7/10 matches an anti-dash kit against a dash-based mage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text carried a fabricated ability and no numbers. Shadow Surge is 140/120/100s at 2000/2500/3000 range, Personal Space 16 -> 12s, Mistral Bolt 8 -> 4s at 1200 range, Looming Darkness 12s flat.
audit.why: The 140s ultimate at rank 1 is exactly why level 6 is your window and why it closes.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into whys[5], mid, spikes[3], ahead and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: FABRICATED ABILITY: 'Doom Arrival' appears in whys[5], whys[6], spikes[1], spikes[3], mid, late and wants.foe[1]. Vex has no such ability — her ultimate is Shadow Surge and her passive is Doom 'n Gloom. It is also described as a 'root' and a 'long-range root that sets up her whole team'; Shadow Surge roots nothing, it marks a target and recasts into a dash. Separately, the fear is mis-slotted: the full layer calls it 'Personal Space (Fear)' throughout, but Personal Space is a 475-range shield and the fear comes from Doom 'n Gloom.
audit.why: Riot text: R 'Fire a missile that marks an enemy champion. Recast to dash to them and deal damage.'; W 'Gain a shield and damage nearby enemies.'; P 'causing her next basic Ability to fear enemies and interrupt dashes'.
audit.corrected: Real names used, the root claim removed, and the fear re-slotted to the passive.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] and late both claim her passive damage 'scales off missing HP percentage'. Nothing in the kit says that; the passive mark is consumed for bonus damage and shortens her empowered cooldown.
audit.why: Missing-health scaling is a specific claim that changes when you take a trade, and it is unsupported.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the mechanic that is in the kit — the dash mark and the empowered-state refresh.

audit.whatIsWrong: No note that her shield eats your burst window.
audit.why: missingInteractions rule shield-absorbs-burst: Personal Space absorbs the charm combo if you commit into it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart disagreed across layers on six of seven rows: win[] reads Vex, Vex, Vex, Vex, Ahri, Vex, Vex while phases[N].side reads Vex, Skill, Skill, Skill, Vex, Skill, Skill — including level 6, where the full layer credited Vex and both win[4] and every content field credit Ahri.
audit.corrected: phases sides aligned to win[] as one atomic group.

edits.before: - Vex Personal Space (Fear): matchup-defining — Shield + AoE fear that punishes dashes — never dash onto her while her passive glows. Check it before every step-up. - R Spirit Rush (last dash) is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - The fear is Doom 'n Gloom, her passive, not Personal Space — while it glows her next ability fears you and interrupts dashes, so Spirit Rush into it is a free kill for her. - Personal Space is a 475-range shield on 16s at rank 1; force it out before you burst.

edits.before: Once her ultimate resets and her item power grows, her passive-driven damage and Doom Arrival threat retake control of the lane.
edits.after: Once Shadow Surge is back up — 140s at rank 1 — and her items land, her passive punish plus that 2000-range mark retake the lane.

edits.before: Doom Arrival's teamfight-defining root plus her anti-mobility kit keeps this her matchup for the rest of the game.
edits.after: Shadow Surge marks from 3000 and dashes her onto you, and her passive interrupts dashes, so she keeps the matchup.

edits.before: Your Spirit Rush finally gives you a way to engage from an angle her passive can't punish as cleanly, letting you get in before she lands Doom Arrival — this is your one clean window in the whole matchup.
edits.after: Your Spirit Rush finally gives you an angle her passive can't punish as cleanly — go while Doom 'n Gloom is on cooldown and before Shadow Surge is up, and this is your one clean window in the matchup.

edits.before: Her passive bonus damage scales off missing HP percentage on top of raw AP, so even after Lich Bane or Shadowflame she still out-trades you if she catches you at half health.
edits.after: Her passive mark converts your dash into bonus damage and refreshes her empowered state faster, so even after Shadowflame she out-trades you whenever you open with Spirit Rush.

edits.before: Doom Arrival is a teamfight-deciding root/burst on top of everything else, and her passive punishing dashes means Spirit Rush actually works against you defensively — this stays her matchup for the rest of the game.
edits.after: Shadow Surge marks you from up to 3000 and dashes her in, and Doom 'n Gloom marks anyone who dashes near her, so Spirit Rush works against you defensively — this stays her matchup for the rest of the game.

edits.before: Level 6 is your one bright spot — Spirit Rush gives you a fresh angle to engage that her stationary passive punishes less cleanly, letting you get in before she sets up Doom Arrival. Use this window to force favorable trades, because it doesn't last: once her ultimate cooldown resets and her item power grows, the lane swings back in her favor.
edits.after: Level 6 is your one bright spot — Spirit Rush gives you a fresh angle that her passive punishes less cleanly, and at rank 1 her Shadow Surge is a 140-second cooldown you can simply out-wait. Use this window to force favorable trades, because it doesn't last: once her ultimate is back and her items land, the lane swings to her.

edits.before: Even once you're itemized, her passive damage scales with your missing HP, meaning low-health all-ins that used to work for you get punished harder against her. Doom Arrival remains one of the best teamfight tools in the game — a long-range root that sets up her whole team. Your best plan is grouping for 5v5s where she has to split attention, since 1v1 dueling her stays lopsided outside your level 6 spike.
edits.after: Even once you're itemized, every dash you take near her leaves a mark she cashes in for bonus damage, so opening a fight with Spirit Rush is punished harder than it should be. Shadow Surge remains one of the best teamfight tools in the game — a 3000-range mark that dashes her onto whoever your team can't protect. Your best plan is grouping for 5v5s, since 1v1 dueling her stays lopsided outside your level 6 spike.

edits.before: Look for Doom Arrival root-into-burst all-ins outside of Ahri's level 6 window
edits.after: Open with Shadow Surge from long range once your level 6 window closes

edits.before: Vex wins by landing Personal Space (Fear), denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Vex wins by fearing you out of your combo with Doom 'n Gloom, then closing from 3000 range with Shadow Surge.

edits.before: Carry through picks — a landed charm is a won fight, and your dashes manufacture charm angles no one wards against.
edits.after: Carry through picks — charm her before she can cash the mark, and Personal Space's shield is her only answer.

edits.before: Ahead, hunt the map: shove with Q, dash-flank every river, and charm-pick Vex's teammates until the lane lead is a game lead.
edits.after: Ahead, shove with Q and roam: Shadow Surge is 140s at rank 1, so until it is up she cannot punish a single rotation.

edits.before: Vex whiffs Personal Space (Fear) and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Vex spends her empowered passive on a minion — that is your window.

edits.before: That is Vex’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Her empowered passive fears you and stops the dash out — never trade into it.

notes: 'Doom Arrival' is not a Vex ability and appeared in seven fields — her ultimate is Shadow Surge and the passive is Doom 'n Gloom. It was also described as a root; Shadow Surge marks and dashes, it does not root. The full layer additionally mis-slots the fear onto Personal Space (a 475-range shield) in focus.text, loading, winCon, dosFull[0], report[1], report[5] and report[9]; I corrected breakdown.cooldowns, enemyWin and dontsFull[0], but LEFT focus.text alone (25 characters, at the applier's skip threshold) and left the report[] and loading strings for a champion-level pass, since the same 'Personal Space (Fear)' focus token drives all of them and changing one without the token would read inconsistently — flagging rather than half-fixing. The 'passive scales off missing HP' claim in spikes[2] and late is unsupported by the kit and was replaced with the dash-mark mechanic that is in it. | COHERENCE: 5 chart edit(s) withdrawn — they moved the row to the enemy while leaving the phase why describing the owner winning it. Chart authority is an open question, so the label was reverted rather than the prose rewritten. Re-propose only as a side+why pair.
